CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Christine is a 63-year-old female presenting for her annual physical examination. She reports doing well overall. Regarding her depression, she has been managed effectively with prescribed medication and weekly therapy sessions, with good compliance and no concerning symptoms. She denies suicidal ideation. She is sleeping well, getting approximately 8 hours per night. Regarding her hypertension, she has been checking her blood pressure at home but reports fluctuating readings over the past couple of weeks, with readings that have been either elevated or low without stabilization. She remains compliant with her blood pressure medication. She reports her diet has been inconsistent lately due to work-related stress and increased work hours, resulting in frequent consumption of frozen meals and limited time for meal preparation. She denies grocery shopping and proper meal preparation. She reports occasional headaches which she attributes to prolonged computer screen exposure at work. Denies headaches with associated swelling. She notes that her carpal tunnel release on the right wrist, performed approximately two years ago, has been doing well with no current numbness or tingling in her hands or fingers.

Denies numbness or tingling in hands and fingers. Denies significant swelling. Otherwise, review of systems is negative.

3. Carpal tunnel syndrome status post right wrist release (approximately 2 years ago)

General: No acute distress. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Neck: No adenopathy, no signs of hyperthyroidism. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs appreciated. Blood pressure: Elevated in office today. Labs: Essentially normal, no abnormalities noted.
